newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs unmoved by Nikkei weakness.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs unmoved by Nikkei weakness.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures failed to gain ground despite the Nikkei's weakness on Wednesday as comments by a Japanese official triggered uncertainty about domestic interest rates.
Chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a parliamentary budget committee that Japan needed to consider measures to deal with the adverse impact low interest rates have on people's incomes.

December Euroyen stood at an intra-day low of 99.18 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.19 on volume of 4,470 lots. June was most actively traded with turnover of 9,600 lots. It was steady at 99.39.
Dealers said the Bank of Japan's generous money market operation provided some support to Euroyen futures.

A trader with a European house said the Japanese interest rate futures were unlikely to be boosted by weakness in Tokyo stocks as most players expected the Nikkei share average to be relatively stable ahead of the Japanese financial year end.
"There was a lot of fund selling of Euroyen. Everybody's expecting the Nikkei to pick up on window dressing before the end of March," he said.
March JGBs settled at 126.45 against their previous 126.40. June was at 124.89 against 124.94.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly easier after some late selling following a drop in U.S. T-bonds.
Dealers said attention would be focused on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's words in the second part of his Humphrey Hawkins testimony late on Wednesday.

They said Eurodollar futures could see some short-covering if his comments were perceived to be neutral following his warning about a pre-emptive interest rate hike in the first half of the testimony last week.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.960 against their IMM close at 93.980 on volume of 5,420 lots.
